exposure: previous problems with bowel evacuation and urgency when going to the toilet
perianal tear grade three or four at first delivery (OASIS)
cohort: The study followed 731 women who gave birth to their first child between May 2009 and December 2010, responding to questionnaires 6 years after delivery.
finding: The prevalence of anal incontinence significantly reduced from late pregnancy to 21% at 6 years after first delivery, and was predicted by older age, high BMI, bowel disease, previous bowel problems, instrumental delivery, and severe perianal tears.
mod_finding: Instrumental first delivery and sustaining a perianal tear grade three or four at first delivery were associated with long-term anal incontinence.
